commit.message:
Commit the whole log prefix when an op reaches a quorum

When the primary received a quorum of PrepareOk messages for op n, it
executed only log entry n-1 and bumped commit_number by one. That
assumes op n-1 was already committed, which is not guaranteed: the
PrepareOk messages for n-1 can all be lost, or the ones for n can
overtake them. In that case the primary executed op n in op n-1's slot,
replied to the client from the wrong state, and later executed op n-1
out of order when its own acks finally arrived. Backups commit strictly
in log order from the commit number in Prepare and Commit messages, so
their state diverged from the primary's.

The paper (section 4.1, step 5) says that a quorum for op n commits n
and every earlier op, and that the primary executes the earlier ones
first. This is safe because backups only acknowledge an op once they
have every earlier op in their log, so the quorum for n is also a
quorum for everything before it. on_prepare_ok now commits every entry
from commit_number up to n, in order, replying to the client for each,
and then drops the ack counters for the committed ops. A PrepareOk for
an op that is already committed is ignored.

Add a cluster test that drops every PrepareOk for op 1 and checks that
a quorum for op 2 commits both ops in order on the primary and, after
a commit heartbeat, on the backups.

Found by the simulator at commit d270079 with:

    SEED=11056962173458606836 cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator

which failed the state-matches-committed-log property at tick 57 with
the primary having applied op 6 at log index 4. With this fix the seed
runs on to tick 78, where it fails on a separate issue: a stale
NewState reply from an earlier state transfer arrives during a later
one and trips the op_number_start assertion in on_new_state.
